articles.title: Power Ranking Every Team in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League
articles.summary: Midweek is about to get exciting again with the return of the UEFA Champions League.
articles.body:
Midweek is about to get exciting again with the return of the UEFA Champions League.

The 36 participating teams in the league phase have finally been confirmed, so it's time to start sorting out the contenders from the pretenders.

What better way to do that than to rank the entire field? We've taken into account last season's performances, European pedigree, difference-making stars and managerial acumen to place each club from worst to first.

Which teams are the most likely to dethrone Paris Saint-Germain? Which are likely to be propping up the table? And which side could spring a surprising run into the latter stages?

Read on for Bleacher Report's UCL power ranking ahead of the tournament's league phase draw on August 27 and then kickoff on September 8.

Think you can do better? Leave your ranking in the comments.

Sabah are preparing for their first-ever appearance in the Champions League. In fact, it's the club's first major European competition after previously failing to get into the Conference League and the Europa League at the playoff stage.

The side from Azerbaijan are less than a decade old, and they are now the second club from the nation to reach the UCL after Qarabag.

It's a massive achievement for the Owls, but getting out of the league phase will be a really tough assignment.

The champions of Slovakia needed extra time in their qualifying matchup against Celje, but they just about squeaked through with a 2-1 victory.

It marks the club's first appearance in the competition since 2024-25, when they finished 35th and couldn't pick up a single point.

AEK Athens snagged their Champions League place with a confident 4-0 second-leg victory over Levski Sofia, returning to the competition proper for the first time since 2018-19.

The squad features a couple of notable veterans. In addition to Croatia legend Domagoj Vida, former Real Madrid and AC Milan forward Luka Jović also represents the Double-Headed Eagles.

LASK have never qualified for the Champions League proper, getting as far as the qualifying round in 2019-20, only to be eliminated by Club Brugge.

But a stunning second-leg comeback over Scottish champions Celtic in qualifying has landed the Black and Whites in the main competition.

A young squad might find it difficult against seasoned veterans on the European stage, but there's something to be said for youthful endeavor, which could lead to a shock or two.

The second of the Norwegian representatives is Viking, an immediate new favorite team for anyone captivated by the iconic rowing among Norway fans at the 2026 World Cup.

Viking might be trailing Bodo/Glimt heading into the final throes of the domestic season, but they are only a point behind with a little less than half the campaign remaining.

It will be a fun side plot of the tournament to see which of the two national rivals finish higher in the league phase.

After a stunning Ligue 1 win in 2020-21, Lille haven't hit those heights since. However, they do enjoy a European jaunt, reaching the UCL round of 16 in 2024-25 after finishing an impressive seventh in the league phase.

Two years is a long time in football, though, and with Ayyoub Bouaddi now a Manchester City player and Matias Fernandez-Pardo potentially on the way out too, there's little hope for a similar stunning finish.

Stuttgart haven't progressed past the opening round of the Champions League since 2009-10. But in their last appearance in the league phase in 2024-25, they were just a point away from qualifying for the knockout playoff.

Coming fourth in the Bundesliga shows there is quality in the squad, providing hope they can go one better this year.

2025-26 Ukrainian Premier League Finish: 1st

Shakhtar Donetsk are once again champions of Ukraine after a surprising drop to third in 2024-25. With that, they are back in the Champions League.

A run to the quarter-finals as in 2010-11 is likely out of the question, with the team having to play their "home" games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge this season because of Russia's ongoing war in the country. An absence of loyal fans will make an already tricky assignment much harder.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: League phase 34th

Czech champions Slavia Praha will at least be aiming for more points than the three they picked up in the UCL last season.

Those came from three stalemates against Bodo/Glimt, Atalanta and Athletic Club, with defeats being dealt by Internazionale, Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur, Barcelona and Pafos.

A single victory against a lower-ranked team would mark an improvement, but it won't secure a trip past the league phase.

A second-place finish in the Dutch league looks great on paper, but Feyenoord were 19 points adrift of PSV by season's end. Meanwhile, a 29th-place finish in last season's Europa League doesn't bring much cause for optimism, either.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst is back in the dugout after a seven-year absence, and avoiding humiliation will be his main goal.

A trip through the qualification stages might not suggest it, but Fenerbahce have quietly built a squad of quality and experience.

Ederson, Milan Skriniar, N'Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku make up a formidable spine, even if some aren't quite at their prime level.

Up against one of the tougher qualification opponents, Marseille, Fener came through with a 3-2 aggregate victory. That experience against a solid opponent will set the Turkish side up well for the league phase.

Lens pushed PSG all the way in Ligue 1 last season, finishing just six points behind their much wealthier and far more talented neighbors to the south.

That success was perhaps a poisoned chalice, with manager Pierre Sage being plucked from the club by Crystal Palace.

Dino Toppmöller is in charge now, and his domestic campaign began with a 5-2 victory over Auxerre. It's a promising start, but European action is a whole different level.

Real Betis are back in the competition for the first time since 2005-06. With wily veteran manager Manuel Pellegrini in charge, Los Verdiblancos have hovered around La Liga's top six for the past five seasons, and they reached the Europa League quarterfinal in the last campaign.

Veterans like Marc Bartra, Hector Bellerin and Isco will ensure the mentality is right when the famous Champions League music plays.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: League phase 35th

Under Marcelino, Villarreal were making steady progress, climbing up the La Liga standings with every passing season.

However, the 61-year-old is now seeking a new challenge, and it's difficult to see the club sustaining those ever-improving standards.

The 2025-26 Champions League campaign saw the Yellow Submarine pick up a solitary point from eight games, finishing a single place off the bottom of the table. It might not get much better in 2026-27.

Cesc Fabregas is back in the Champions League, but this time, he's entering the competition as a manager.

The Spaniard has done a fantastic job at newly flush Como, a club that was in the Italian second tier just two years ago.

While expectations should be tempered, livewire Nico Paz has the ability to make magic happen, and that could lead to some surprise results.

In what will be their first-ever appearance in a European tournament, I Lariani will make club history one way or another.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Round of 16

The darlings of the 2025-26 Champions League, Bodø/Glimt are back for another round of giant-killing.

After picking up draws with Tottenham Hotspur and Borussia Dortmund in the league phase, the Norwegians concluded the stage with wins over Atletico Madrid and Manchester City, jumping into the knockout playoff round in 23rd place.

But they weren't done there. They then dispatched of Internazionale with victories in both legs, winning 5-2 on aggregate. While a 3-0 first-leg victory over Sporting CP in the round of 16 set them up for another historic result, the Portuguese side won 5-0 after extra time in the second leg to close the book on the fairytale run.

The Eliteserien leaders will draw renewed attention this time around, and they've earned a sizable boost in the power ranking as a result.

After a year away from the competition, RB Leipzig are back in the UEFA Champions League, with dreams of equalling the club's best finish—a semifinal berth in 2019-20.

Former Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Manchester City center-back Martin Demichelis is now in charge, and he'll be bringing his experience as a player in the tournament to the dugout. Departures of star players Yan Diomande and Lois Openda immediately make his task difficult, though.

Manager Gian Piero Gasperini consistently had Atalanta performing well above expectations during his nine-year stint. It seems he's now repeating the trick with Roma.

The Giallorossi finished third in Serie A last season, their highest finish since the 2017-18 campaign. That secured a return to the Champions League for the first time since 2018-19, and the side from the Italian capital should not be underestimated.

Gasperini took Atalanta to the UCL quarterfinals in 2019-20, a fine example of the 68-year-old's capabilities in the competition.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: League phase 30th

After securing a Serie A title in 2024-25, Napoli were expected to make swift progress through the following Champions League campaign.

However, the Antonio Conte second-year curse kicked in, and the Partenopei could only manage a 30th-place finish in the league stage. Of course, they also couldn't keep hold of their Serie A title, and Conte has since departed for pastures new.

Massimiliano Allegri is now at the helm, and the decorated manager is in the hunt for his first European title.

Expect Napoli to be much more competitive this time around, at least progressing past the league phase.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: League phase 28th

It's three Eredivisie titles in a row now for PSV and manager Peter Bosz, whose 28th-place finish in the UCL last time out paints over some impressive results.

In a tough gauntlet of fixtures, the side from Eindhoven claimed a 6-2 home win against Napoli and thrashed Liverpool 4-1 at Anfield.

But that was their only two victories from eight, with defeats to Union SG, Atletico Madrid, Newcastle United and Bayern Munich ultimately ending their campaign at the first stage. Just one more point would have been enough to extend their European run to at least another round.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Knockout playoffs

Belgian Pro League champions Club Brugge snuck into last season's Champions League knockout playoff partly thanks to a well-deserved 3-3 home draw with Barcelona.

While they secured the same result against Atletico Madrid in the first leg of the first elimination round, a 4-1 loss in the repeat fixture at the Wanda Metropolitano sent them packing.

Still, a domestic title and a decent performance in the 2025-26 UCL give them a solid mid-table place for now. With genuine European pedigree arriving in the form of goalkeeper Yann Sommer, the club might be eyeing a round-of-16 spot.

Porto lost just twice on the way to the Primeira Liga title last season, winning the Portuguese top flight for the first time since the 2021-22 campaign.

Defeat in the Europa League quarterfinals to Nottingham Forest was undoubtedly disappointing, but manager Francesco Farioli had lost leading scorer Samu Aghehowa to injury by that point, making the task much more difficult.

The 22-year-old forward could be back in action by November, which might boost Porto's chances of climbing up the league phase table.

In power ranking terms, Os Dragões get a handy lift because of their league finish. If they can translate that form into European action, they could climb higher in no time.

Manchester United rode the Michael Carrick wave all the way to third spot in the Premier League last season, resulting in a Champions League return after a year away from the competition.

But we've seen this story play out before. A temporary manager brings a short-term bounce in results, and after getting the job permanently, things start to unravel. The signs of the tale repeating were evident in the Red Devils' 2-0 loss to newly promoted side Hull City on the opening day of the season.

Still, there is strength in the squad, headlined by Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo. United should handle the lower-ranked teams in the competition with ease, and the 14th spot here might seem a little harsh. However, with other teams having achieved more in European action last season, they can't yet climb much higher.

Galatasaray always carry an aura of danger about them in European competition. Rams Park is a terrifying venue to play at, and the home fans can make the situation oppressive for any opposing team.

After a fourth Super Lig title on the bounce, it's clear which team is the one to beat in Turkey. Meanwhile, in European matters last season, the Lions earned wins over Liverpool, giant-killers Bodø/Glimt and Ajax in the league phase before sending Juventus packing in the knockout playoff.

Gala can beat any team on its day, and with a striker like Victor Osimhen to deal with, defenses simply cannot let their guard down against the Turkish giants.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: N/A (Europa League winners)

The final days of the summer transfer window will be crucial for Europa League champions Aston Villa, who have been stripped for parts.

Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne have all departed Villa Park, while Ollie Watkins might soon be following. That dramatic loss of talent showed in a 4-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion in their Premier League curtain-raiser.

While the initial wave of replacements looked impressive, more is needed to bring Villa back to a level capable of challenging both domestically and in Europe. Unai Emery has proved adept at building competitive teams in European tournaments, but at the moment, the task appears too much to handle.

The Villans should just make it through the league phase, but they won't get much further. Until proven otherwise, though, they take a fairly high spot in the power ranking thanks to winning the Europa League last season.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Quarterfinals

Liverpool are a really hard side to pin down at the moment. After last season's disaster, the club decided to swap Arne Slot for Andoni Iraola, and the Spaniard has the unenviable task of trying to make the $300 million duo of Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, who arrived last season, work.

Things at least looked promising in their Premier League opener against Newcastle United. While the Reds needed a last-minute penalty to secure a draw, the play was much more positive than in Slot's final months in charge, although defensive frailties remained.

The Champions League will offer the squad more time to get attuned to Iraola's methods, which might lead to a slow start and gradual improvement the longer they stay in the competition.

The Merseysiders have automatically qualified for the last 16 in the last two Champions League campaigns, but doing so this time around might be out of the question. A run to the quarterfinals last season gives them a perhaps undeserved 11th spot in the power ranking as things stand.

Borussia Dortmund disappointed in the Champions League last season, tumbling out of the competition at the knockout playoff round after a stunning second-leg comeback from Atalanta.

But a second-placed finish in the Bundesliga was their best since 2022-23, and it looks like the Schwarzgelben will again be the closest challengers to Bayern Munich's domestic dominance.

The league phase shouldn't cause too much bother, and Serhou Guirassy guarantees goals. A step further in the competition this season should be well within reach.

Sporting CP's run to the Champions League quarterfinal last season was a memorable one.

Os Leões squeezed into an automatic round-of-16 spot at the last gasp, and they then secured a sensational aggregate win against Bodo/Glimt at that stage, overturning a 3-0 first-leg deficit with a 5-0 win in the second outing.

They came unstuck against finalists Arsenal, but they certainly made the Gunners work for it.

Sporting gets a hefty bump in the rankings because of that effort. Manager Rui Borges is still at the helm, and he'll try to replicate the formula this time around.

Some key players have left, such as Morten Hjulmand, Ousmane Diomande, and Francisco Trincão, but they've so far managed to keep hold of Luis Suarez, who scored five goals in the competition last season.

It's all change at Manchester City. Pep Guardiola has left the Etihad Stadium after 10 years in charge, with Enzo Maresca arriving to take the Catalan's well-worn seat in the dugout.

The Italian was perhaps a bold choice to take over, having comparatively little experience as a club manager. However, he was schooled under Guardiola's tutelage, perhaps making the transition a little easier.

But it's still a big challenge to replace one of the best football managers in history, and the scale of the task was illustrated in a nervy 2-1 win over Bournemouth in the opening Premier League fixture of the season.

He won just three of his six Champions League games while in charge of Chelsea, although one of those was an impressive 3-0 victory over Barcelona.

The 46-year-old has immense talent at his disposal at City, but the jury is still out on whether he can get the best from those players.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Semifinals

Atletico Madrid surprisingly made the Champions League semifinals in 2025-26, with manager Diego Simeone proving he can still extract every last bit of ability from his players in European competition.

That reputation alone makes Los Rojiblancos dangerous in Champions League matches. However, their ultimate success this season might depend on whether Julian Alvarez sticks around (and whether he can be integrated back into the team if he does).

Even so, Simeone will drag his team through the league phase one way or another. Going on a deep run can never be ruled out, either.

Serie A title holders Internazionale will be desperate to avoid a repeat of their disappointing exit at the knockout playoff stage last season.

The 2024-25 finalists finished a comfortable 10th in the league phase only to crash out to an upstart Bodo/Glimt side.

Manager Cristian Chivu still achieved a league and Coppa Italia double, though, perhaps proving that the exit to the plucky Norwegian team was an unfortunate blip. In his second season in charge, he'll be better versed in how to handle the competition.

Elite forward Lautaro Martinez is still around, and the club has strengthened with mostly English talent, including John Stones, Djed Spence and Curtis Jones. Those arrivals don't do that much to move the needle, but they at least provide greater squad depth with Champions League experience.

As domestic title winners, they get a boost in the power rankings despite their lackluster showing in the UCL last time out.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

Real Madrid, the most decorated team in Champions League history, are running it back, with former manager Jose Mourinho returning to his old stomping grounds.

The Portuguese has won two European Cup titles during his decorated career, but neither of those came with Los Blancos. It's something that will be high on his agenda as he leads the club for a second time.

The summer has seen some high-profile arrivals at the Santiago Bernabéu, including Yan Diomande, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konaté and Carlos Espi. With players like Kylian Mbappé, Vinicius Junior and Jude Bellingham already at the club, there are few squads in the competition that are quite as formidable.

Whether Mourinho still has the managerial acumen to make them all click is another matter. The 63-year-old hasn't won a league title since 2014-15, and his last Champions League winners' medal came in 2009-10. His conservative style of play also might not suit a squad full of virtuosos.

This iteration of Real Madrid is perhaps the most interesting squad in the tournament. Progression to the knockouts seems like a given, but what they do from there is anyone's guess.

Bayern Munich lost to eventual champions Paris Saint-Germain in the semifinals last season, which is nothing to be ashamed of. The 5-4 defeat in the first leg was one of the finest games the competition has ever seen, so neutrals will be tuning in to the Bavarians' matches hoping for more of the same.

The club's firepower remains, courtesy of Harry Kane, Luis Diaz and Michael Olise, and another Bundesliga title looks a near certainty. If it's another canter in domestic action, Vincent Kompany can fully throw the club's weight behind the pursuit of a first European Cup since 2019-20.

Even if ultimate success isn't achieved, Bayern's UCL campaign should at least be entertaining.

La Liga champions Barcelona will be among the clutch of favorites to win the competition.

The Blaugrana have made a splash in the transfer market this summer, bringing in Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Joao Cancelo and Rodri. That last signing alone gives them a significant new edge, with the Spaniard the finest defensive midfielder on the planet.

A little more protection for the back four gives Lamine Yamal and Raphinha increased license to do what they do best in the attacking third without worrying about what's going on behind them. The loss of Robert Lewandowski strips them of a focal point up front, but in Gordon, they've signed a player who scored 10 in the competition for Newcastle United last season.

It might all come together for Barça in Europe this season, with manager Hansi Flick seeking to add a second Champions League winners' medal to his collection.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Runners-up

While Arsenal broke their 22-year Premier League title drought in 2025-26, they couldn't end their long wait for a European Cup.

The Gunners lost in the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties, coming agonizingly close to a trophy that has so far eluded them.

In the 2026-27 tournament, the North Londoners have to be considered among the favorites to win, and at least to make the final. Mikel Arteta has built on an already stacked squad, investing in quality and depth that should help them compete across multiple competitions.

The Champions League will surely be a priority this season, and after falling at the final hurdle last time, the players will use that experience as fuel to go one better.

2025-26 Champions League Finish: Winners

Who can stop this Paris Saint-Germain side from winning a third Champions League title in a row?

The Parisiens have the luxury of taking it easy in their domestic league, with few challengers on their way to the Ligue 1 trophy. That means manager Luis Enrique can rotate top stars at will, keeping them fresh for European competition.

In the past two Champions League campaigns, PSG have finished outside of the automatic round-of-16 qualification spots in the league phase. While that's put additional games on their schedule, that hasn't been an issue. In both cases, the French side got stronger as the competition progressed, culminating in back-to-back titles.

It's perhaps a risky strategy, but it has served Enrique's side well so far. When you have a squad packed with elite talent, including Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Vitinha, João Neves, and Desire Doué, you can trust that they can bring a performance when it really matters.

PSG again have a target on their backs, but when it gets to the knockout stages, few have been able to hit it.

articles.title: Chelsea 5-2 Real Sociedad: Melvine Malard double helps move Blues to brink of Women's Champions League league phase
articles.summary: Report as Melvine Malard scores twice in Chelsea's 5-2 win over Real Sociedad in first leg of Women's Champions League third qualifying round; Naomi Girma, Veerle Buurman and Lauren James also on target
articles.body:
Ainhoa Marin opened the scoring for the visitors in the seventh minute before a goal ultimately credited to Naomi Girma from Katie McCabe's corner drew the sides level.

It was 2-2 after Veerle Buurman and Cecilia Marcos both scored in the span of four second-half minutes, then Malard, who joined the Blues from Manchester United in July, fired Chelsea back in front in the 67th minute.

Lauren James extended their lead seven minutes later and Malard added her second with two minutes remaining.

Assistant coach Camille Abily took charge of Chelsea in the absence of Sonia Bompastor, who was serving a suspension held over from last season.

The visitors took the lead when Marin curled a spectacular shot from range over Hannah Hampton, and Sandy Baltimore nearly drew the sides level but caught the underside of the crossbar.

Chelsea were finally back on level terms in the 29th minute. It looked as though McCabe might have scored it herself but the goal was given to Girma, who it was determined had glanced it on.

Buurman directed James' corner past Julia Arrula nine minutes after the restart but Chelsea's advantage proved short-lived after Marcos equalised, giving Hampton no chance when she fired into the far corner.

Malard made it 3-2 when she rounded the keeper and slotted home seven minutes after the hour before James added a 74th-minute cushion, tapping home after some great build-up play by Ellie Carpenter.

Substitute Malard, who replaced Beever-Jones 10 minutes into the second half, then latched onto a pinpoint Carpenter cross to ensure Chelsea will travel to Spain with a healthy aggregate advantage.

articles.standfirst: Los de Mourinho buscan contrincantes para su asalto al trono del PSG
articles.summary: Los de Mourinho buscan contrincantes para su asalto al trono del PSG
articles.body: El Real Madrid afronta con optimismo el sorteo de este jueves de la fase liga de la Champions. Como siempre la dificultad crecerá en función de los rivales que toquen de los bombos 2, 3 y 4. Roma, Dortmund y Manchester United aparecen como los más difíciles en el segundo; Nápoles, Fenerbahce y Leipzig son complicados en el tercero mientras que Como, Stuttgart y Lens aparecen como rivales con más enjundia en el cuarto. Como en la temporada 25-26, el formato de la Champions 'obliga' a los 36 equipos a disputar ocho partidos, dos contra rivales de cada uno de los cuatro bombos, uno de ellos en casa y otro fuera. Como máximo, el Real Madrid se puede enfrentar a dos equipos del mismo país y no puede jugar ni contra Barcelona, Atlético, Betis ni Villarreal.

articles.title: Así es el sorteo de Champions League 2026-27: cómo funciona, bombos, reglas y formato
articles.standfirst: La UEFA consolida su revolucionario formato con la participación de 36 equipos encuadrados en una liga única
articles.summary: La UEFA consolida su revolucionario formato con la participación de 36 equipos encuadrados en una liga única
articles.body: La edición 2026/27 de la UEFA Champions League mantiene el renovado modelo de competición estrenado dos temporadas atrás. En lugar del clásico formato por grupos, los 36 clubes participantes disputarán una primera fase compuesta por ocho jornadas únicas en un ranking unificado. El Sorteo de la Fase de Liga se celebrará este jueves 27 de agosto a partir de las 18:00 horas. Para agilizar el proceso y evitar bloqueos entre países, la UEFA emplea un sistema híbrido que combina la extracción manual de bolas con un algoritmo informático encargado de asignar los rivales. Los clubes participantes quedan divididos en cuatro bombos según su coeficiente individual, reservando siempre la primera plaza del Bombo 1 al vigente campeón. Cada equipo disputará cuatro partidos como local y cuatro como visitante, midiéndose obligatoriamente contra dos adversarios procedentes de cada uno de los cuatro bombos. Finalizada la liguilla, los ocho primeros clasificados accederán directamente a los octavos de final. Por su parte, del noveno al vigesimocuarto puesto disputarán una eliminatoria previa de play-off, mientras que los clasificados entre las posiciones 25 y 36 quedarán eliminados definitivamente sin opción de acceder a la Europa League. Sigue todo el sorteo a través de MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Savinho vuelve a ser Sávio
articles.standfirst: Debut, gol y asistencia en la goleada del Tottenham sobre el Charlton Athletic (5-1) en la Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Debut, gol y asistencia en la goleada del Tottenham sobre el Charlton Athletic (5-1) en la Carabao Cup
articles.body: El cambio de Savinho a Sávio en su camiseta venía a reflejar la intención del brasileño por volver a ser el extremo que enamoró en las filas del Girona. De momento, le ha sentado bien tras debutar con el Tottenham marcando gol y repartiendo una asistencia en la goleada contra el Charlton Athletic (5-1) en la segunda ronda de la Carabao Cup. Ya que estuviese en la convocatoria escasos días después de fichar procedente del Manchester City supuso una gran sorpresa. Ahora bien, como es lógico, arrancó desde el banquillo. Las bandas fueron para Mathys Tel y un Mikey Moore que fue el gran protagonista de la primera parte. A menos de cinco minutos para el descanso, marcó a pase de Bentancur y asistió a Solanke en el 2-0. En el 65' ingresó Pedro Porro en el terreno de juego y, sólo dos minutos después, Danso hizo el tercero para el Tottenham a pase de Mateus Fernandes. Solanke, poco después, dejó su puesto a un Savinho que apenas tardó 10' en estrenarse como goleador con los 'spurs'. Agarró el balón en banda derecha, 'surfeó' por el pico del área y remató al palo corto. No se quedó ahí el brasileño y, aunque con un poco de fortuna, asistió a Ben Davies para cerrar la 'manita'. La última vez que fabricó dos goles fue contra la Juventus en el Mundial de Clubes del año pasado. Lloyd Jones, eso sí, la 'empañó' anotando el gol de la honra para el Charlton Athletic. El Everton no tuvo demasiados problemas para quitarse de encima al Preston North End (0-4). Thierno Barry se lució anotando un 'hat-trick' y Brennan Johnson cerró la goleada marcando su primer gol con los 'toffees'. Mucho más tuvo que sufrir el Newcastle, que presentó a Nico González en la previa, para eliminar al West Brom (3-2). Bazoumana Touré hizo el primero y, en la segunda parte, Harvey Barnes resolvió.

articles.title: No. 1 Overall Recruit Jalen Brewster Makes Decision on Recruitment After Texas Tech Commitment
articles.summary: After committing to Texas Tech in the fall, class of 2027 top recruit Jalen Brewster has assured the Red Raiders he isn't going anywhere.
articles.body:
After committing to Texas Tech in the fall, class of 2027 top recruit Jalen Brewster has assured the Red Raiders he isn't going anywhere.

He told Rivals' Hayes Fawcett that he is shutting down his recruitment.

"I feel like Texas Tech is the best place for me and the best place to build my own legacy," he said.

Brewster, a Buford, Georgia, native, is considered to be the No. 1 overall player in the class of 2027 by 247Sports' composite rankings . He held offers from virtually every top program in the country but picked Texas Tech over Indiana and Ohio State.

Brewster, who stands at 6'3" and 302 pounds, joins a stacked class of 2027 for the Red Raiders. Texas Tech's defensive line in particular should be in good shape, as No. 3-ranked edge Anthony Sweeney has committed to Joey McGuire's program.

The Red Raiders have the eighth-ranked class for 2027, according to 247Sports .

Texas Tech is one of the teams to watch this year and in the coming years in college football. The Red Raiders finished 12-2 last year, marking one of their best seasons in program history as they reached the College Football Playoff for the first time.

Texas Tech is rumored to have one of the strongest NIL funds in college football, and the evidence is in the Red Raiders' loaded recruiting and transfer portal classes.

But having talent doesn't always equal winning championships. McGuire, who is in his fourth season in Lubbock, will look to prove he's the coach who can bring Texas Tech a national title in the near future.

Once Brewster arrives on campus, winning a championship should be made much easier.

articles.title: Big 12 ADs Ban Pros from Returning to School After Big Ten, SEC Rule Changes
articles.summary: Big 12 athletic directors agreed to ban professional athletes from returning to schools in the conference across all sports on Wednesday:
articles.body:
Big 12 athletic directors agreed to ban professional athletes from returning to schools in the conference across all sports on Wednesday:

ESPN's Pete Thamel first reported the news.

Thamel previously reported that ACC athletic directors met on Wednesday with "momentum" for the ban of NFL players returning to the college football landscape.

On Tuesday, the Big Ten passed a rule banning any player who declared for the NFL draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a pro league from returning to football teams within the conference.

The SEC also announced the implementation on a similar ban that extends to men's and women's basketball players.

Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger previously reported that the Big 12 was considering a league-wide policy that banned professional players from returning to the conference.

On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that tight end Dae'Quan Wright had committed to play for LSU for the 2026 season after he was waived by the Cleveland Browns. Former Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris also agreed to become a member of the Tigers once he was waived by the New Orleans Saints.

Wright and Harris were among the athletes that were granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court that made them eligible to return to college athletics.

Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris previously expressed his disapproval of players participating in NFL training camps before returning to the college football landscape.

"Yeah, I think it's just one of those things, like, what are we doing right now? It's just one more thing we're putting on the list, and that, quite frankly, we don't have time to deal with and figure out what the rules are and what's going on," Morris said, per 247Sports' Scott Wright .

"At some point, I think there's got to be some integrity in this game," he added. "There has been forever, that goes along with sports in general, and playing these, and we've taught this from the youth sports up. If a guy's competing for a professional job right now in this sport, he should have left college in the back mirror at that point."

Now, professional athletes in all sports won't be permitted to return to college and suit up for Big 12 schools.

articles.title: Nico Gonzalez: 'Mini Rodri' shown he will be loved at Newcastle
articles.summary: Nico Gonzalez is given a rapturous welcome before Newcastle's Carabao Cup win against West Brom following the £52m midfielder's arrival from Manchester City.
articles.body:
Nico Gonzalez wanted to feel loved. He quickly got his wish at St James' Park on Wednesday night after completing his £52m move from Manchester City .

Newcastle United 's new signing was handed a rapturous welcome before he even kicked a ball for the club as supporters repeatedly chanted his name.

The sight of Gonzalez walking out at the sold-out stadium before the 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup second round was a welcome one for head coach Matthias Jaissle, who desperately wanted him.

The German stressed he was "always a believer in the positive things", but tellingly also referred to the pursuit as a "long fight".

Having spoken personally to Gonzalez on a number of occasions, Jaissle made it clear how much he wanted the 24-year-old and how pivotal he would be in his side.

"It's always important if you're making signings like Nico that there is a commitment there," Jaissle said.

"But he showed that from the beginning, from our first conversations."

Newcastle face Millwall in third round - full draw

A lot has clearly changed since Gonzalez first set foot in the Premier League a year and a half ago and made his Manchester City debut against Newcastle . Of all teams.

Before City's 4-0 win, the new arrival had been warned about the intensity Newcastle 's midfielders played and pressed with at their snarling best.

But the unfazed Spaniard ended up completing a staggering 100 passes, and helped snuff out any potential breakaways from the visitors at Etihad Stadium.

It was a glimpse of the skillset - in and out of possession - which convinced Manchester City to sign defensive midfielder Gonzalez from Porto for £50m.

City's then manager, Pep Guardiola, even labelled him "our mini-Rodri" in the absence of his influential, injured team-mate.

Gonzalez ultimately found an extended run of starts hard to come by once his compatriot returned to full fitness, though.

But former Manchester City assistant manager Kolo Toure believes he will have benefited from his experience at the Etihad.

"When you are in competition against players like Rodri, you learn a lot because you come up against them in training and you have to show the manager you are better than them," he said.

"You learn from things they do as well and, on the ball, he learned a lot from Rodri. Without the ball he's really good because he can press, get it back and read the game really well.

"He has this capacity to steal the ball from opponents, which is top. He's better than Rodri at this in my opinion, but Rodri on the ball is the best in the world.

"Both of them have different qualities and different strengths."

'He'll keep improving because of his mentality'

Gonzalez had a close relationship with Rodri and long humbly recognised that only a select number of players can start in his position at clubs bidding to challenge for the biggest honours.

Rodri was that man at Manchester City under Guardiola and, following the midfielder's move to Barcelona, new manager Enzo Maresca has signed Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , having already brought in Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest .

The club also look set to make a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez .

It was still not easy for Gonzalez to leave Manchester City , where he felt settled, but Newcastle will give him the platform he has been longing for as a key player.

The enthusiastic Spaniard sees this as an opportunity to develop further, which has always been a driver.

"His mentality is top," Toure said. "I would review games individually with the players and every time I had my laptop and sat next to him, he was so open to learning.

"He wanted me to show him and I wanted to help him because he was demanding in that way.

"You want to have players like this because they want to see what they do well and not well, and are open to criticism.

"He's going to keep on improving because of his mentality."

Gonzalez certainly did so when he left Barcelona, where his professional career started, and has such experience to fall back on.

Having spent a decade at Barca, and risen through the ranks, Gonzalez ultimately had to depart to truly flourish elsewhere.

Following a successful loan spell at Valencia, he joined Porto on a permanent basis at the age of 21 before earning a move to Manchester City .

Former Barcelona B team-mate Roger Riera feels he has developed "another vision" as a result.

"Nico has seen different countries and different styles of football," he said. "He's added a lot of things to his game, which have made him a more complete player.

articles.title: Barcelona vs Athletic Club: La Liga – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha will seek to add to Barcelona’s five-star La Liga opener when Athletic arrive from Bilbao.
articles.body:
Who: Barcelona vs Athletic Club What: Spanish football’s La Liga Where: Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain When: August 27, at 9pm local time (19:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream.

Barcelona aim to go back-to-back to start their search for a threepeat in La Liga when Athletic Club arrive on Wednesday.

The Catalan giants are riding high after consecutive league titles – and opened their league season with a win – while rivals Real Madrid have languished for the last two seasons.

Their visitors from Bilbao will not be a walkover, especially with all eyes on Barca’s hunt for a striker in the transfer market.

What is the latest on Barcelona’s pursuit of Julian Alvarez?

Barcelona coach Hansi Flick indicated Wednesday the club may end the summer transfer window without signing a new striker if they fail in their bid to lure Argentinian star Julian Alvarez from rivals Atletico Madrid.

The Spanish champions are still pursuing 2022 World Cup winner Alvarez but Atletico have thus far refused to sell the 26-year-old forward, who missed training on Wednesday due to illness.

Spanish media reported Barca president Joan Laporta wants “Alvarez or nobody” and Flick said the club also had to think about the future and he is happy with his squad.

“I don’t want to speak about Julian. I only want to (speak) about the situation of the club. We made some really good, good transfers now in this market,” the German coach told reporters.

“Our goal is clear, but in the end also the club has to think about the future. Not only the present now.

“Of course as a coach I will say ‘OK, give me the best you can have, and more and more and more’ – maybe it works or maybe not. I have total confidence with the quality we have now.”

What has been the story of the chase for Alvarez?

In July, Laporta said Barcelona had made a bid for the Atletico forward and the club were leaving it on the table even after Atletico told them Alvarez was not for sale.

Laporta reiterated later Wednesday that Barcelona are still hoping Atletico decide to sell them Alvarez, who was jeered by the Rojiblancos’s own fans during their 2-2 La Liga draw against Villarreal on Sunday.

“It seems that the player wants to come to Barca, and therefore we continue to hold on to our hope, our intention – always with the utmost respect for Atletico Madrid – of being able to sign the player,” Laporta said in a video broadcast by the club.

Laporta said Barca had received “information” that Atletico had been in talks with other clubs about the possibility of selling Alvarez, with the president keen for the striker’s destination to be Camp Nou if he does leave the Spanish capital.

Arsenal have been linked to Alvarez in recent days, while Real Madrid made a bid for the striker at the start of the summer, although it was not seen as a serious attempt to sign him.

“We would like to reach an understanding with Atletico Madrid – we maintain our proposal, our offer to Atletico Madrid,” continued Laporta.

“Hopefully there will be an understanding between the two clubs, between all of us, so that if they sell the player Barca will be the ones that can acquire the services of Julian Alvarez.”

Barca cruised to a 5-0 win against Elche on Sunday in their La Liga opener, with Raphinha and Fermin Lopez scoring twice each and Anthony Gordon setting up two goals on his debut.

Barca’s display was a clear warning to rivals Real Madrid and their new coach, Jose Mourinho, that the Catalans will not relinquish the title easily.

Karim Adeyemi also found the net on his debut as Barca made light work of a vulnerable Elche side at the Martinez Valero stadium.

Athletic were beaten 3-1 at home by Sevilla to open their season in La Liga on Saturday.

Yuri Berchiche was sent off for Athletic in the 11th minute, before Oso, Chidera Ejuke and Isaac Romero put Sevilla 3-0 up by the hour mark.

Aitor Paredes scored a consolation for the Bilbao-based club.

What happened the last time Barcelona played Athletic Club?

Barcelona squeezed a 1-0 La Liga win in Bilbao in their last meeting with Athletic.

Lamine Yamal scored the only goal of the game midway through the second half.

Barca dominated the possession in that encounter, but Athletic edged the shots on goal.

What happened in the corresponding game between Barcelona and Athletic Club?

Barcelona stormed to a 4-0 in November in this same game last season.

Robert Lewandowski, Fermin Lopez and a Ferran Torres brace saw off the visitors, who had Oihan Sancet sent off in the 54th minute – by which point his side were already three goals behind.

When did Athletic Club last beat Barcelona?

Athletic’s last win against Barcelona came in the Copa Del Rey with a 4-2 victory in January 2024.

Lewandowski and Yamal had turned the game to give Barca the lead after Gorka Guruzeta opened the scoring in the first half.

Sancet levelled early in the second period before Inaki Williams and Nico Williams sealed the win in extra time.

When did Athletic last beat Barcelona in La Liga?

Athletic have not recorded a league win against Barcelona since August 2019 when they emerged with a 1-0 win in Bilbao.

Aritz Aduriz scored the only goal of the game, with just a minute left on the clock, in what was the season opening game for both clubs.

The Opta supercomputer has given Barcelona a 66 percent chance of winning the match, while Athletic are only afforded a 15 percent chance.

There have been 249 meetings between the sides, with Barcelona winning 128 times and Sociedad claiming 81 victories.

Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji both remain long-term absentees with knee injuries.

Gavi is also struggling with a knee injury and remains a doubt, while Rodri’s fitness is likely to keep him sidelined still.

articles.title: Tottenham 5-1 Charlton: Jamie Redknapp praises Savio after goalscoring debut as Roberto De Zerbi challenges new signing
articles.summary: Savio made an immediate impact on his Tottenham debut, coming off the bench to score and grab an assist against Charlton; Jamie Redknapp was full of praise for the Brazilian, but Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi challenged his new man to build on his stunning start
articles.body:
Savio, who joined the club on Tuesday in an £85m move from Manchester City , instantly made himself a fan favourite just over 24 hours after his arrival by scoring and grabbing an assist during a 20-minute cameo in Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton.

The Brazilian brought excitement and flair with every touch, and despite only scoring once in the Premier League last season, showed some much-needed end product for a Tottenham team who netted just 48 times themselves.

His brilliant introduction earned praise from former Tottenham midfielder Redknapp, who claimed the 22-year-old was exactly the type of spark fans want at the club.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Watch FREE PL highlights

"He lit the place up," Redknapp said post-match.

"This is what Tottenham want. Players like that who can get you off your seat. Who can cut inside and hit a ferocious left footed shot. He was excellent."

However, despite making an immediate impression, Spurs boss De Zerbi challenged his new man to take the next step.

Prior to his debut, De Zerbi detailed what Savio needed to do to become one of the best wingers in the world, and doubled down on that after the game.

"Yes, it is a perfect day for him," De Zerbi said of Savio.

"I think his biggest step and biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals because as qualities, I think he is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals.

"I spoke with him and we put the goal on 10 or 12 goals (target) because we need 10 or 12 goals from the wingers.

"Last season we suffered too much because also the number of goals were not enough to compete for nothing more than that (17th) position."

Savio gives Spurs the hope their front line needs

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"A lot can happen in just one minute of football. Even more can happen in 20. As we have just seen, that's enough time to make yourself a cult hero.

"Savio's arrival at Tottenham was shrouded in question marks. Why were Spurs willing to part with so much money for a player who managed just three goal contributions in the Premier League last season?

"Yet, the moment he stepped out onto the pitch in a white shirt, he was a livewire. Spurs fans value entertainment, and they were off their feet any time he got on the ball.

"The fact there was some end product that came with the excitement is even more important, especially for a Spurs side that have often been lacklustre in attack.

"The opponents will get tougher, and Savio will need to rise to that. However, as first outings go, having joined barely 24 hours ago, you can't ask for much more."

Alabama Little League World Series star Cam Lee isn't the first athlete in his family to represent the state on a big stage.

The Phenix City center fielder is the younger brother of former Crimson Tide linebacker Markail Benton, another Phenix City product who starred at Central High School before signing to Alabama .

Lee even played a small role in Benton's recruitment story. When Benton announced his commitment to Nick Saban and the Crimson Tide in June 2016, his little brother helped reveal the decision during the ceremony.

Markail Benton stats with Alabama football

Benton was a four-star linebacker and one of Alabama's top in-state prospects in the 2017 recruiting class. He played in 23 games over two seasons with the Crimson Tide and totaled 33 tackles before transferring to Jacksonville State .

Lee has his own aspirations of attending Alabama, but his dreams aren't for the diamond. He wants to quarterback Alabama football's offense, according to the ESPN broadcast.

Ten years after helping his brother announce where he would play college football, Lee is having his own moment in the spotlight, starting in center field for Phenix City's run at the Little League World Series.

articles.title: QB Tommy Castellanos commits to No. 12 Texas Tech with court-granted 5th season of eligibility
articles.summary: Well-traveled quarterback Tommy Castellanos plans to play this season for No. 12 Texas Tech, the Big 12 favorite that is set for returner Will Hammond to be...
articles.body:
LUBBOCK, Texas (AP) — Well-traveled quarterback Tommy Castellanos plans to play this season for No. 12 Texas Tech , the Big 12 favorite that is set for returner Will Hammond to be its starter after transfer Brendan Sorsby was declared ineligible this summer because of gambling.

Castellanos told ESPN on Wednesday he had committed to the Red Raiders . On the quarterback's verified X account, in which the bio included the phrase professional athlete, there was a photo posted later in the day with him in a Texas Tech uniform.

The decision came after Castellanos last Friday was among 10 athletes granted a temporary restraining order by a Kentucky judge to get a fifth season of college football. The NCAA announced a rule change in June allowing players who began college in 2023 or later to have five years to play five years of sports in college.

Castellanos, a freshman at UCF in 2022, went undrafted by the NFL four months ago before a tryout as a receiver with the Miami Dolphins during their rookie minicamp.

He had declared for the NFL draft last December after dropping his appeal for another year of college eligibility . The NCAA had denied his waiver request to play another season at Florida State

Castellanos transferred to Florida State following two seasons at Boston College. His fifth game at UCF as a freshman was the American Athletic Conference championship game after the starter got hurt.

In 38 college games, Castellanos has completed 477 of 816 passes (58.5%) for 6,449 yards with 48 touchdowns and 28 interceptions. He was 180-of-309 (58.3%) for 2,760 yards, 15 TDs and nine interceptions last year in his 12 games for the Seminoles.

Hammond played in eight games for Big 12 champion Texas Tech behind graduated Behren Morton last season before an ACL injury on Oct. 25. After no setbacks in his recovery, Hammond has been part of fall camp. The Red Raiders open the season at home Sept. 5 against FCS team Abilene Christian.

Sorsby transferred to Tech in January after two seasons at Cincinnati , and was expected to start instead before an NCAA gambling investigation and since-dropped lawsuit over his eligibility.

articles.title: Champions League Draw 2026-27, Schedule of Dates for League Phase Fixtures
articles.summary: The teams taking part in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League were set after qualifying rounds concluded on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The teams taking part in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League were set after qualifying rounds concluded on Wednesday.

36 squads will be part of the league phase before teams in positions 25 to 36 are eliminated in Jan. 2027.

Teams were placed into four pots based on their UEFA club coefficients on Wednesday.

Here's a look at the schedule of dates for the 2026-27 Champions League.

Knockout Phase Playoffs: Feb. 16-17 and Feb. 23-24

Quarterfinals: April 6-7 and April 13-14

The exact opponents that each team will face during the league phase will be determined during Thursday's draw.

Beginning with the first pot, teams will be drawn against two opponents in each of the four pots until eight opponents are selected for the schedule. The draw moves to the other three pots in order until the entire league phase is finalized.

However, a team cannot play the same individual league phase fixture for three seasons in a row under new UEFA regulations.

The first pot automatically featured the reigning Champions League winner, Paris Saint-Germain, as the team looks to capture a third consecutive Champions League title.

PSG is attempting to become the fourth club to win the UEFA Champions League three straight times and the first since Real Madrid accomplished the feat in 2018.

Arsenal is a strong contender to emerge victorious after narrowly falling to PSG in the 2026 final. Arsenal put together a dominant 2025-26 run despite being unable to win a title, winning all eight league-phase matches.

Barcelona is also entering the Champions League with high expectations following a hard-fought defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid in the quarterfinal round last season.

articles.title: La Champions se pone en marcha... con un sorteo más favorable para los españoles
articles.standfirst: William Hill sitúa a Barcelona y Real Madrid entre los cinco favoritos a ganar la competición
articles.summary: William Hill sitúa a Barcelona y Real Madrid entre los cinco favoritos a ganar la competición
articles.body: Ya se conocen los 36 equipos que compondrán la fase liga de la Champions 26-27 después de finalizar unas largas rondas previas. Esta misma tarde tendrá lugar el sorteo que descubrirá qué ocho rivales le corresponden a cada equipo en esta primera fase del torneo, que vuelve a poner en marcha la competición de clubes más importante de Europa. España contará, al igual que la temporada pasada, con cinco representantes y, a priori, el sorteo debería ser algo más amable que el del pasado curso. La principal diferencia respecto a la edición anterior está en la distribución de los equipos españoles. Este año no habrá ningún representante en el Bombo 4, mientras que tres partirán desde el Bombo 1, uno desde el Bombo 2 y otro desde el Bombo 3. Barcelona, Real Madrid y Atlético de Madrid compartirán el primer bombo con los grandes transatlánticos del fútbol europeo. Un escenario que también tiene su reflejo en las apuestas deportivas, donde los dos grandes favoritos españoles aparecen con opciones reales de pelear por el título. A pesar de quedarse en cuartos de final la temporada pasada, William Hill mantiene al Barcelona y al Real Madrid entre los grandes candidatos a conquistar la Champions. El conjunto azulgrana cuenta con una cuota de 7.5, mientras que la del Real Madrid asciende ligeramente hasta los 8.0. Ambos se encuentran dentro del Top-5 de favoritos. Una consideración que contrasta con la del Atlético de Madrid, que aparece bastante más atrás con una cuota de 29.0. Los de Simeone parten, por tanto, con un escenario más complicado para aspirar a levantar la Orejona. Otro de los representantes españoles será el Betis, que regresa a la Champions más de 20 años después y lo hará desde el Bombo 2. El conjunto verdiblanco afronta una fase liga especialmente ilusionante después de haber conseguido clasificarse para la máxima competición continental más de 20 años después y William Hill le asigna una cuota de 67.0 para proclamarse campeón. La misma cuota recibe el Villarreal, que volverá a partir desde el Bombo 3 después de quedarse fuera en la fase liga de la pasada temporada. Las mejores casas de apuestas ya han establecido sus primeras diferencias entre los cinco representantes españoles. Ahora sólo queda esperar al sorteo para conocer el camino de cada uno. Barcelona y Real Madrid parten con la etiqueta de candidatos... pero el primero objetivo de todos es firmar un pleno en esta primera fase. El nuevo formato volverá a exigir regularidad desde el primer partido y, con 36 equipos en busca de los 16 billetes (ocho directos y otros ocho en 'playoffs') para las eliminatorias, cualquier detalle puede terminar siendo decisivo.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola transfer news: Liverpool reach £120m deal in principle for PSG forward
articles.summary: Liverpool have reached a £120m deal in principle to sign PSG forward Bradley Barcola; deal not finalised yet but major breakthrough in talks; there has been a gap in valuation between two clubs throughout summer, with PSG asking for around £145m for Barcola
articles.body:
The deal has not been finalised, with last details still being discussed, but there has been a breakthrough in negotiations.

There had been a gap in valuation between the two clubs throughout the summer, with PSG previously asking for around £145m for the France international.

The final detail of the proposed deal is still to be agreed but the £120m fee is understood to now be fixed in place as the value Liverpool will be paying for the 23-year-old.

Should Barcola complete his proposed transfer to Anfield, he would be Liverpool's second most expensive signing of all time, following the club-record deal to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle for £125m last summer.

The signing of Barcola would take their overall spend since the end of the 2024/25 season to just over £663m, after also spending £116.5m on Florian Wirtz as well as signing Milos Kerkez, Hugo Ekitike, Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet, Giovanni Leoni and Jeremie Frimpong.

Should Liverpool get this deal over the line before the deadline, it would allow Cody Gakpo to leave Anfield, with Tottenham and Manchester City both interested in the Dutchman.

Liverpool are also trying to sign a second new winger, with their target currently Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr following difficult negotiations with Brighton for Yankuba Minteh .

Liverpool have approached Palace over a potential deal for Sarr.

Andoni Iraola's side are considering their options after talks stalled with Brighton over Minteh. Brighton are holding out for £80m after rejecting two bids from Liverpool, the latest worth £60m.

Meanwhile, Palace have no intention of letting Sarr go at this stage and consider the 28-year-old to be not for sale. He has three years left on his contract.

Sarr missed Palace's opening weekend defeat at Everton. Reports claimed he was refusing to train but it is understood that the winger is currently injured.

Carra: I'd love Barcola at Liverpool - but they need to replace Salah!

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes that Barcola is not the profile of player Liverpool should be prioritising, despite admitting he would be a "great" signing for the club.

The former defender has said Liverpool should be prioritising the signing of a right-winger to replace Mohamed Salah after the Egypt forward left the club at the end of last season.

Barcola predominantly operates off the left wing but has feature on the opposite flank during his time at PSG.

"He's a great player, there's no doubt about that - I'd love to get Barcola at Liverpool," Carragher told Sky Sports News . "But he's a left winger for me.

"Liverpool's big thing that stands out like a sore thumb right now is replacing Mo Salah, a right winger. And I don't think Liverpool have got anybody really in the squad who looks fully comfortable playing right wing.

"They probably have at least four players in the squad before Barcola joins, if he joins, who could play on the left-hand side comfortably.

"Now, I'm not saying any of those players are better than Barcola. But in terms of the balance of the squad, it's not the position Liverpool need right now. They need a right winger.

"But if you're saying to me, do I want Barcola to come and Liverpool are going to sign a right winger as well? I'll be absolutely delighted because players would have to move on. Of course they would.

"But right now, I felt this summer would be about replacing Mo Salah. Barcola doesn't replace Mo Salah."

articles.title: Chaos mars Fenerbahce’s Champions League qualifying win over Lyon
articles.summary: Fenerbahce’s French midfielder Guendouzi was attacked by Lyon fans after he mocked them at the end of the match.
articles.body:
Goals from Vedat Muriqi and English defender Archie Brown helped Fenerbahce stun Lyon in the Champions League playoffs and qualify for the league phase in a fixture marred by ugly scenes as the Turkish team’s midfielder Matteo Guendouzi taunted the home fans.

French international Guendouzi was attacked by Lyon fans at the end of the match on Wednesday after he celebrated his team’s 2-1 win in a manner that seemed to provoke the home fan base at the Groupama Stadium.

It led to clashes between players and coaching staff on and off the football pitch, and the visiting team’s celebrations descended into chaos.

When the match got under way, the teams were locked at 1-1 from the first leg in Istanbul a week ago, but the Turks opened up a 2-0 lead on the night in the first half in southeastern France.

Exciting Belgian winger Malick Fofana gave Lyon hope in the second half, but Lois Openda and Kail Boudache had further strikes ruled out for offside, and Fener held on.

Hungarian Barnabas Varga scored a brace, and former Real Madrid forward Luka Jovic added another as AEK Athens cruised into the league phase with a 4-0 thrashing of Levski Sofia.

Romanian Razvan Marin added a penalty as the Greeks booked their progress following a 0-0 draw in the first leg in Bulgaria.

Viking Stavanger hit back from a goal down on the night to beat Dinamo Zagreb 3-1 in Norway to progress 5-3 on aggregate.

They will play in the Champions League group phase for the first time.

Albanian Arber Hoxha gave Dinamo an early lead, but Zlatko Tripic equalised from the penalty spot just eight minutes later.

Two goals in two minutes early in the second period from Edvin Austbo and Tobias Moi sealed Viking’s progress.

Panama’s Cristian Martinez scored the extra-time winner as Slovan Bratislava qualified for the Champions League group phase for the second time in three seasons.

Two years ago, they lost all eight games but finished second from bottom in the single league phase on goal difference above Young Boys.

Andraz Sporar had given the Slovaks an early lead at Celje, but Svit Seslar equalised for the Slovenians from the penalty spot.

Martinez bagged the winner on the night for a 3-2 aggregate success for Slovan.

articles.summary: Entra por Arnau… con la duda del mediocentro entre Koke y Cardoso
articles.body: Segunda prueba de Simeone de cara al partido del sábado contra el Sevilla. Una prueba en la que el argentino ha estrenado pareja de ataque con Lookman. El nigeriano formó en punto con Giuliano, que podría ser la solución a las ausencias de Sorloth, lesionado, y Julián, que por segundo día seguido no se ejercitó con el grupo al estar indispuesto. El resto del equipo lo formaron Oblak, en portería, con Llorente y Grimaldo en las bandas. Pubill y Hancko estuvieron en el eje de la defensa. La medular, con Giuliano arriba, fue para Kang-in Lee y Baena en los costados. Barrios es fijo en la medular y el puesto de 5 empezó con Cardoso y acabó con Koke. “Correr para atrás”, insistía Simeone durante la segunda sesión de la semana. Sabe el argentino que el Pizjuán será una dura prueba y quiere que todos estén enchufados como se vio en el penúltimo entrenamiento antes de medirse al Sevilla. La buena noticia fue la presencia del Cuti en el partido. El argentino, que trabaja para ponerse al ritmo de sus compañeros, completó la sesión con los suplentes. El mejor ejemplo de que cada vez está más cerca el estreno del ex del Tottenham.

articles.title: Yaya Touré hace historia en la Champions: primer entrenador africano en lograrlo
articles.summary: El costamarfileño ha escrito una nueva página en la historia del fútbol africano. Tras la clasificación del Slovan Bratislava frente al Celje, el exjugador del Barcelona y Manchester City se convierte en el primer entrenador africano en dirigir a un equipo en la fase de liga de la Champions League, la antigua fase de grupos.
articles.body: El costamarfileño ha escrito una nueva página en la historia del fútbol africano. Tras la clasificación del Slovan Bratislava frente al Celje, el exjugador del Barcelona y Manchester City se convierte en el primer entrenador africano en dirigir a un equipo en la fase de liga de la Champions League, la antigua fase de grupos. Un logro histórico que llega después de que el conjunto eslovaco superara la eliminatoria y sellara su presencia entre los grandes de Europa. Touré vivió la clasificación con una enorme celebración junto a sus jugadores, protagonizando unas imágenes de vestuario que reflejan la magnitud del momento. El nigeriano Ndubuisi Egbo ya había hecho historia en 2020 al convertirse en el primer entrenador africano en dirigir a un club en la Champions, al frente del KF Tirana, aunque entonces el equipo no consiguió alcanzar la fase final de la competición.

articles.title: Benjamin Weber interview: Augsburg sporting director is a former Chelsea analyst overachieving in the Bundesliga
articles.summary: In this exclusive interview, Benjamin Weber, a former analyst under Thomas Tuchel at Chelsea, discusses his decision to pursue a new path that has seen him step out of the shadows to become sporting director at FC Augsburg. "It was always Thomas. I could hide..."
articles.body:
Weber worked as an analyst for Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Chelsea. He describes that period at Stamford Bridge as the best of his life. "To win that title was absolutely amazing. I don't want to make my part too small, nor too big."

Most would have stayed, gone on with Tuchel to Bayern Munich and beyond. Weber, now 43, embarked on a different path. "When you are fighting for the Champions League and finally you win it, what else is there to come? You always need an objective."

As a result, Weber left to become managing director of Paderborn. "I told Thomas. It was tough." And in 2025 he took on a new role as sporting director of Bundesliga club Augsburg. "I don't work just to work. I was curious enough to do something different."

Augsburg are a relatively modest outfit compared to some of Weber's previous employers but they are a major success story in Germany. Their stay in the Bundesliga now extends to 16 consecutive seasons. "And there are only [six] other teams who can say that."

But last season, Weber's first, was a particular triumph for Augsburg. It was their first top-half finish in a decade. They managed it despite - or perhaps because - the decision was made to change coach midway through the campaign. It was a big call to make.

"It was very difficult," Weber acknowledges. "And emotional because I have been sat on the other side of the table. I know how it feels. It would be easy to hide but I am there to make decisions even if it is tough. We needed something different to get back on track."

Out went Sandro Wagner and in came Manuel Baum instead. Augsburg turned their season around. "We had problems with results and performance but not development. In the end, we were ninth, after many changes last summer, and it worked out."

For Weber, after the glamour of Paris and London, he is now seeing the other side of football in more ways than one. "On the one hand, there was a lot of pressure at the bigger clubs. On the other, for me personally, it was always Thomas. I could hide," he admits.

He had a taste of this at Paderborn. "When you sign a player and you know that the club will only survive if it is the right player, that is pressure. When you lose your job at a small club, and you have a family, that is pressure." At Augsburg, his profile is higher.

"There is more focus on me personally now. I was always a little bit the hidden guy in football. Now I came a little bit into the light. Not the biggest stage, I do not need that. But when we have success, I am part of it. And when we do not, I am also part of it."

The feeling is that he got his first major decision right. Maybe even more right than he had realised at the time. Baum had been an internal appointment, taking the job on a temporary basis with the intention of returning to his role as director of development.

Baum is now the permanent head coach. "Plans can change," says Weber. "He had an open mind. We did not know if it would work out and he would go back to his old role but in the end we all felt comfortable with this. It is human to change your perspective."

In Weber, the hope is that Augsburg have a sporting director who can see it from all perspectives. "I did analysis my whole life. For sure, I can bring this into our recruitment so maybe this is an advantage. And I know how coaches think. Maybe that helps too."

But how far can that take a club like Augsburg? Around 30,000 fans fill the WWK Arena for each game, an impressive number but unremarkable by Bundesliga standards. What does being ambitious look like for a club that appears to be punching above its weight?

"What is maybe unique is that we are stable," says Weber. Stable does not sound sexy but nor does it mean standing still. There is an understanding that Augsburg need to keep improving. Being perceived as Bundesliga perennials can help make this possible.

"Players love to come to Augsburg, this is a good first step," he explains. "We want this unique selling point in the sense of developing players. We want to build more of a connection to the youth academy as well. This is what we want the club to stand for."

Rodrigo Ribeiro's loan from Sporting has been made into a permanent transfer after a promising season. Hennes Behrens has signed from Hoffenheim. Sima Suso comes in from Fortuna Dusseldorf. All three are aged 21. Augsburg as a home for talent.

In backing potential, dare they aim higher? "You need not to be crazy, but to dream a little bit, have a vision," says Weber. "In England, you will know the Sunderland story, the Brentford story, so many good stories." Maybe Augsburg can be that story in Germany.

"We need work ethic, character. With that, it can bring the best out in you and you can hunt to get to the top. We have to want to hunt together and be good hunters. Then we can maybe go step by step." It is a different target these days. But Weber is relishing it.

"In the end, I have the feeling it was a good decision."

articles.title: Lotte Wubben-Moy and Mariona Caldentey exclusive: Focus clear as Arsenal look to 'right the wrongs' of past WSL title challenges
articles.summary: Lotte Wubben-Moy and Mariona Caldentey talk exclusively to Sky Sports ahead of the new WSL season; Arsenal get their WSL campaign under way against Brighton at the Broadfield Stadium  on Sunday September 6, kick off 12pm
articles.body:
"We want to go and win the league," mdifielder Mariona Caldentay told Sky Sports .

"The WSL title is definitely the trophy we are eyeing up," added defender Lotte Wubben Moy.

It's been a long wait for the Gunners to add to their four WSL titles. Their last came back in 2019 and Arsenal are not hiding away from the ambition of ending that drought.

"We know the fans want the WSL title as much as we do," Wubben-Moy told Sky Sports .

"We want to add to Arsenal's 15 titles."

Caldentay added: "I'd love to win all of the titles, of course, but the league is a big focus for us.

"We have been missing consistency but if we can find that, we'll be close to winning the league.

"You need to be good in every game to finish first in the league.

"That's really hard to do but that is our mentality now. That is what we want to do."

On the diffiucty of winning the title, she added: "It's something we are really working towards but then there is so much competition now.

"There are so many good teams now and they are also signing good players this summer. The league gets better every year and that is so good for the competition.

"We now have such good teams, players, stadiums and facilities. That is so good for women's football."

Gunners ready to 'right wrongs' of slow starts

Arsenal finished four points behind winners Man City last season and while the Gunners won the inaugural Champions Cup, they did not retain their Women's Champions League title and also exited the FA Cup at the quarter-final stage and the League Cup in the semi-finals.

A slow start in the league, which has become a bit of a trend for Arsenal in recent season, once again proved costly for Rene Slegers' side.

Wubben-Moy is aware a fast start could be crucial to Arsenal's title ambititions and is ready to "right the wrongs" of previous campaigns.

"We have had a good six to seven-week pre-season," the England international said. "That's a luxury in our game and it's a great opportunity to build with the players we already have and build on what we've already got. We can then integrate the new players into that.

"We all want the build up in the rear-view mirror and to get going with the season. While I'm excited for this building stage and growth, I'm ready to write the wrongs of the past.

"I'm an experienced player and I have been here in the moments where we have struggled in the first part of the season, and it is definitely something we can improve."

With Arsenal looking to hit the ground running this season, they did plenty of their summer transfer business early.

It's been a summer of change with seven players coming in starting with England midfielder Georgia Stanway, who has been joined by experienced internationals Selina Cerci, Geraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle, Misa Rodríguez, Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm.

When asked if the new faces in the squad have brought excitement ahead of the new season, Wubben-Moy said: "Without a doubt. We have added a lot of quality and experience, and a lot of character. They are joining a squad with a lot of character already so it will add a lot of depth, which is exciting.

"I'm pretty experienced within football now so with that, there's inevitable change. That's not just individuals but also infrastructure, investment and engagement.

"The women's game continues to grow so quickly, so much so that you have to be nimble, adding characters and the quality we have this summer, it allows us to be even more nimble.

"As an experienced player within the squad - I have been here a good while now - I feel I can add a bit of guidance and help provide an environment where new players do come in and feel comfortable and are able to grow and progress."

Caldentey excited to build Stanway partnership

Stanway in particular was eye-catching business from Arsenal as they captured the 27-year-old from Bayern Munich on a free transfer.

Caldentey has faced Stanway plenty of times at international level and in recent seasons for Arsenal against Bayern Munich, but she is now extremely excited to be team-mates.

"I have played against Georgia a lot at international level and also when we have faced Bayern Munich," Caldentey said.

"I have a lot of respect for her as a player and I am very happy to have her on my side now.

"You can already see in training that we will have a really good connection and I am looking forward to building that.

"She will help the team a lot and I hope I can help her too."

On the other additions this summer, she added: "You can see the quality of the players coming in straight away in training.

"With Georgia, you can see she likes the ball and is a good passer. She's a baller and that will be really good for us."

It's not just additions this summer at Arsenal with the Gunners losing experienced players such at Beth Mead and Katie McCabe.

Laia Codina, Victoria Pelova and Manuela Zinsberger have also left the club and while Caldentey is aware of the experience departing the club, she believes it is also an opportunity for the different players to strep up and fill the void left behind.

She said: "We've lost a lot of experience with big players with big characters leaving, but that is football.

"People leave and people come but we need to adapt quickly and find new roles.

"We have enough experience in the players we have signed. Some of them are quite young but they are already ready. We have a good balance.

"When players leave that is a new opportunity for other players.

"We have a really good squad but hopefully everyone can step up again so that we can have a really good season."

'Fans could play crucial role in title challenge'

Memories of last season are still fresh with the Arsenal men's and women's victory parade around north London where hundreds of thousands of supporters lined the streets to celebrate a first Premier League title in 22 years for the men, and the women showing off the inaugural Women's Champions Cup they won against Brazilian side Corinthians in February round off a successful club campaign.

They were special times for Wubben-Moy, who believes the connection the team have with the fans could be a significant factor in their own bid to win the title for the first time since 2019.

"I think back to being a young girl and filling the stadium as a fan, but I also think about the stadiums we have filled in the last two to three years," she said.

"We need to understand that as players, we have a duty to serve the fans.

"The men's team feel the same way so to see a moment where we can celebrate with those people we gladly serve and see them out on the streets of north London, seeing all the joy was amazing.

"I saw a lot of friends out that day on the route and on the bus stops. It was incredible.

"We already have a great connection with the fans but something like the parade, it creates an even deeper connection. It's definitely a positive for us and an advantage as a club because we have such a deep connection with the fans, the streets and the people."
